tickets.detail: Note (fedora1-onboard-7): DIAGNOSED (not fixed), routed to #parallax. Level 2 can never load, on any platform. ete.plax stores its region name as 'Ã©tÃ©' (code points c3,a9,74,c3,a9: the UTF-8 bytes of 'été' read as cp1252), while desktop/assets/ete.atlas (UTF-8) declares 'été'. libGDX reads an atlas through FileHandle.reader(), which uses the platform default charset. In 2019 that was cp1252 on Windows/Java 8, so the atlas also came back as 'Ã©tÃ©' and the names matched. Since Java 18 (JEP 400) the default is UTF-8 everywhere, so atlas.findRegions('Ã©tÃ©') is empty and .get(4) throws 'index can't be >= size: 4 >= 0'. WagonLevel.init swallows it, and setAsGameReady then fails on 'Asset not loaded: game/wagon/wa2/WAGON.png', which is a red herring. The other three .plax files use ASCII region names (parallax1, Automne1-4, parallax4) and are fine. Nothing catches it: ParallaxAssetTest checks only atlasName, and GameRunTest draws only level 1. Fix options for whoever takes it: (a) rename the region to ASCII 'ete' in BOTH ete.atlas copies AND re-serialise ete.plax with the pinned kryo 5.0.0-RC1 and the same register() order (check ete.plaxpj too); (b) rewrite the atlas's region line as 'Ã©tÃ©' in UTF-8, which needs no code but is ugly; (c) in WagonLevel, read the page through GVars_Serialization, repair the names, then Parallax_Heart() + setPage. Whichever it is, extend ParallaxAssetTest to check that every regionName#regionPosition exists in the ROOT atlas (TextureAtlasData pars

tickets.title: Every carriage change leaks a SpriteBatch and a ShapeRenderer: nextLevel calls GVars_Camera.init()
tickets.detail:
core/src/jks/vue/models/game/GVars_Game.java nextLevel() calls GVars_Camera.init() inside the fade, to put the camera back at the start of the carriage. init() also does staticBatch = new SpriteBatch() and shapeRenderer = new ShapeRenderer() and never disposes the old ones, so each carriage (and each loop back from the ending, r60) leaves a batch's mesh + shader and a renderer's behind on the GPU. Fix: split the camera reset (camera.position.x = WORLD_WIDTH/2, or setToOrtho again) from creating the renderers, and call only the reset from nextLevel. Seen while fixing r64; not changed there. Proven by LevelWalkTest / LevelFadeTest still passing, and a check that GVars_Camera.staticBatch is the same instance before and after nextLevel.

Commit 30-char summary below; hash in the first line.

Commit 47cee1a (not pushed). GVars_Camera.init() now builds the SpriteBatch and the ShapeRenderer only if they don't exist yet. It then calls the new resetCamera(), which makes a fresh 1600x900 camera at the start of the carriage. GVars_Game.nextLevel calls only resetCamera(), so a carriage change no longer leaves a batch's mesh and shaders and a shape renderer behind on the GPU. That includes the loop back from the ending. tickets.title: Apply d8: Credits is fine
tickets.detail:
Simon settled doubt d8, and it needs writing.

THE DOUBT: The menu font cannot write 'Crédits': desktop/assets/ui/fonts/OptimusPrinceps.ttf, the face behind GVars_Font.labelStyle_ScreenTitle, has no é (U+00E9), and its É (U+00C9) does not draw either. Found while applying d6: I translated the start menu's last two English words, rendered it and looked, as the #ui pack says to. 'Quitter' is fine. 'Crédits' comes out 'Cr¨dits' — FreeType leaves a bare accent where the letter should be — on the button AND on the credits screen's own heading (Index_Credits.TITLE). In caps it is no better: 'CRÉDITS' renders 'CRDITS' with a floating acute. Renders of both attached. The font's coverage is German/Nordic (ä æ ö ø ü ß) and it is missing é è à â ç, so this will bite again the next time an accented French word goes into a title. Everything in GeosansLight takes accents fine, which is why 'Résolution' and 'Simon Bédard' look right. I left the word as 'Credits' with the reason written next to it — defensible, since the face draws everything as capitals and unaccented capitals are ordinary French typography — but it is your game's typography, not my call.
THE QUESTION: Leave the menu reading 'Credits' — which is how French capitals are normally written anyway — or should the menu font be made able to spell 'Crédits', by patching the missing glyphs into OptimusPrinceps.ttf or by using a different face for the menu?
HIS DECISION: Credits is fine

tickets.title: Correct 'no source survives' for parallaxReader0.7.jar, and point ParallaxAssetTest at the atlas the game actually loads
